description:
Recorded as a PROPOSAL. Do not execute a deletion from this bead.

A proposal to delete crates/nee_soon was raised. The numbers behind it were WRONG and the deletion looks unsafe as scoped. Recording the corrected picture so the proposal can be judged honestly.

CLAIMED: 1,005 lines, ~95% doc comment wrapped around two `pub use` statements.
ACTUAL (measured 2026-08-07):
- 1,005 total lines across 7 files (lib.rs 177; xin_wang_sp3_workflow/ mod.rs 204, case.rs 163, sp3_multiphysics.rs 141, mesh_mc.rs 115, mgxs.rs 103, validation.rs 102).
- 490 non-comment non-blank lines -- 49%, NOT ~5%. The claim was off by about an order of magnitude.
- It is not "two pub use statements". Those exist (lib.rs:61-62, re-exporting NordheimFuchsExactTimestepper and TehOPrkeError), but lib.rs:59 also declares `pub mod xin_wang_sp3_workflow;` -- a 6-file, 828-line module with ~40 public items (XinWangSp3Workflow, MgxsGenerationStage, MeshMonteCarloStage, Sp3MultiphysicsStage, Fig429ValidationStage, Mk1DesignPoint, ControlRodRemovalTransient, digitised Fig-4.29 reference curve, 8-group energy structure), plus pub struct NeeSoon (lib.rs:95) and its real pass-through new_prompt_excursion_model (lib.rs:111-129).

WHAT IS fairly criticised: all four workflow stages are stubs returning WorkflowError::NotYetImplemented (mgxs.rs:97-102, mesh_mc.rs:109, sp3_multiphysics.rs:135, validation.rs:96). So it is real STRUCTURE with no physics -- a different and much weaker criticism than "95% comment around two re-exports".

DEPENDENTS (deletion breaks all of these):
- crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/Cargo.toml:17
- crates/tampines/Cargo.toml:60  <-- a SECOND dependent the workspace CLAUDE.md does not mention; fix that doc gap regardless
- root Cargo.toml:19 (member) and :288 (workspace dep)
- live use in 3 example trees: tampines/examples/fhr_sim_v2/app/prke_backend/mod.rs:5,588; digital-twin-engine/examples/fhr_sim_v2/app/prke_backend/mod.rs:5,588; digital-twin-engine/examples/htgr_sim_v1/{app/schematic.rs:44, physics/kinetics.rs:36}

RECOMMENDATION: do not delete. Either finish the four workflow stages (they belong to the op-fr2.2 Xin Wang SP3 epic) or shrink nee_soon to the re-export shim its dependents actually use -- but that is a decision for the maintainer, not a cleanup.
title: PROPOSAL (corrected): do not delete nee_soon — numbers behind the proposal were wrong

description:
Batched **golden-section search** (golden-ratio 1-D minimisation) across the
three backends. There is no golden-section implementation in the crate today —
this is new code, in `src/math/` or a new `src/optimise/`.

Why it is wanted: derivative-free bracketed minimisation of a scalar function
on `[a, b]`, for the cases where a root-find is the wrong tool (minimising a
residual, a limiter blend factor, a property-inversion objective that is not
monotone).

What to deliver:

- Serial reference: classic golden-section with the fixed `(3 - sqrt(5)) / 2`
  contraction, a stated bracketing precondition (unimodal on `[a, b]` — say
  loudly in the doc that a non-unimodal input gives *a* local minimum, not
  *the* minimum), and both absolute and relative interval tolerances.
- **Batched** form: N independent brackets contracted in lockstep. Golden
  section is uniformly convergent and branch-free, so this is one of the
  cleanest GPU fits in the whole epic — the interval count after k iterations
  is identical in every lane.
- Optional Brent-style parabolic-interpolation variant as a CPU-only faster
  path; do **not** put it on the GPU, its branching kills the lockstep
  property that makes the batched version worth doing.

V&V: analytic minima of smooth test functions with known answers, plus the
theoretical contraction rate (interval width should shrink by the golden ratio
per iteration — assert it). Record the measured numbers per the workspace V&V
documentation rule.
title: outram-foam-basic-lib: golden-section (golden-ratio) 1-D minimisation, batched on the hybrid backend
